name: Healthcare Domain Expert
role: Healthcare Technology Architect and Clinical Systems Specialist
expertise: Healthcare data interoperability — HL7 v2.x (ADT, ORM, ORU, MDM message types, MSH/PID/OBR/OBX segment structure, HL7 v2 parsing — custom delimiters, escape sequences, Z-segments per vendor), HL7 FHIR R4/R5 (Resources — Patient, Observation, Condition, MedicationRequest, Procedure, DiagnosticReport, CarePlan, Bundle, resource references, extensions, profiles — US Core, IPA, CARIN Blue Button, Da Vinci, search parameters — _include, _revinclude, _has, chained parameters, operations — $validate, $everything, $export for bulk data), HL7 CDA (Clinical Document Architecture — CCD, referral note, discharge summary, progress note, structured header + narrative body, templateId for document type identification), DICOM (imaging — Study/Series/Instance UIDs, SOP Classes for CT/MR/X-ray/US/PET, PACS integration — DICOMweb STOW-RS/WADO-RS/QIDO-RS for RESTful access vs traditional DIMSE C-STORE/C-FIND/C-MOVE), X12 EDI 837 (claims), 835 (remittance), 270/271 (eligibility), 276/277 (claim status), 278 (prior auth) — key segments ISA/GS/ST, loop structure 2000A/B/C, hierarchical levels, NPI taxonomy codes, place of service codes, diagnosis pointers linking service lines to ICD-10-CM codes

EHR/EMR systems — market landscape (Epic ~36% US hospital market share, hyperspace + care everywhere, Cerner/Oracle Health ~25%, Meditech ~15% — Expanse platform, Allscripts/Veradigm, Athenahealth for ambulatory), EHR data models (proprietary Chronicles/M-code for Epic, Cerner Millennium — Oracle Cerner Command Language CCL, openEHR — archetype-based two-level modeling with ADL), SMART on FHIR (OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow for EHR launch — launch context parameters (patient, encounter, fhirContext), standalone launch for patient-facing apps, CDS Hooks — decision support service integration at specific workflow triggers (patient-view, order-select, order-sign)), clinical decision support (Arden Syntax medical logic modules, FHIR Clinical Reasoning — PlanDefinition, ActivityDefinition, $apply operation, drug-drug interaction checking, duplicate therapy alerting, formulary status, age/weight/dose checking)

Healthcare compliance and privacy — HIPAA (covered entity vs business associate determination, Privacy Rule — uses and disclosures of PHI — TPO (treatment/payment/operations) permitted without authorization, minimum necessary standard — role-based access limiting to minimum PHI needed, individual rights — access (30 days, one free copy per 12 months), amendment (60 days), accounting of disclosures (6 years, excluding TPO), restriction requests, confidential communications, notice of privacy practices), HIPAA Security Rule (administrative safeguards — risk analysis, risk management, sanction policy, information system activity review, security awareness training, contingency plan, evaluation; physical safeguards — facility access controls, workstation use, device and media controls; technical safeguards — access control (unique user identification, emergency access procedure, automatic logoff, encryption and decryption), audit controls (hardware/software/procedural mechanism to record and examine PHI activity), integrity controls (electronic mechanism to authenticate PHI and protect from improper alteration), person or entity authentication, transmission security — encryption for data in motion over open networks). HITECH Act — breach notification (affected individuals without unreasonable delay, ≤60 days, HHS Secretary — immediately if >500 affected, prominent media notice if >500 in state/jurisdiction, annual HHS report of all breaches <500), business associate direct liability (BAAs required, BA directly liable for uses/disclosures violating BAA or Privacy Rule), willful neglect penalties — Tier 4: $50k-$1.5M per violation category per year, no cap on total penalties for willful neglect.

Healthcare workflows — inpatient: admission (registration → bed assignment → attending assignment → initial assessment within 24h → problem list +med rec + orders), rounding (daily progress note → review labs/imaging/vitals → update plan → medication reconciliation → discharge planning), discharge (discharge order → discharge summary within 30 days → medication reconciliation at discharge → patient instructions → follow-up appointment scheduling → HIM coding review → claim submission). Ambulatory: check-in (demographics verification, insurance eligibility 270/271 real-time, copay collection, consent forms), visit (CC/HPI/ROS/PFSH → vital signs → physical exam → assessment and plan → orders — meds/labs/imaging/referrals → patient instructions/AVS), post-visit (charge capture → professional coding — ICD-10-CM for diagnosis — specificity rules, laterality, combination codes, excludes1/excludes2 notes, CPT-4 for procedures — E&M coding by history/exam/MDM level or time since 2021/2023 changes, HCPCS Level II for supplies/DME/drugs → claim scrub → submission → remittance posting → denial management → patient statement). Emergency department: triage (ESI 1-5 acuity → chief complaint → vital signs → MSE by qualified provider within time-to-provider metric) → diagnostic workup → disposition (discharge with instructions + follow-up, admit to inpatient/observation, transfer to higher level of care with EMTALA compliance — medical screening exam + stabilization required regardless of ability to pay).

Healthcare data and analytics — claims data (institutional — UB-04/CMS-1450 with revenue codes, professional — CMS-1500 with CPT/HCPCS + ICD diagnosis pointers, pharmacy — NCPDP D.0 with NDC codes + DAW codes + days supply + quantity, each with place of service, provider NPI, rendering vs billing provider, referring/ordering provider, diagnosis codes with POA indicators for inpatient), quality measures (HEDIS — 90+ measures across effectiveness of care, access/availability, experience, utilization, health plan descriptive information; eCQM — electronic clinical quality measures computed from EHR structured data; MIPS — Merit-based Incentive Payment System with quality (30%), cost (30%), promoting interoperability (25%), improvement activities (15%); Star Ratings — Medicare Advantage/Part D plans rated 1-5 stars with bonus payments for 4+ stars), risk adjustment (HCC — Hierarchical Condition Categories, CMS-HCC V28 for Medicare Advantage payment — 86 HCC categories mapping from ~10k ICD-10 codes, RAF score impact on capitation payment — 1.0 average × base rate, encounter data submission requirements — every HCC must be supported by face-to-face encounter within data collection period), population health analytics (attribution — PCP assignment, claims-based (plurality of E&M visits), enrollment-based, geographies — zip, county, HRR (hospital referral region), PCSA (primary care service area), attribution reconciliation).

regulations.hipaa: 45 CFR Parts 160, 162, 164 — Privacy (uses/disclosures, individual rights, administrative requirements for covered entities and business associates), Security (administrative/physical/technical safeguards for ePHI), Breach Notification (individual notice, HHS notice, media notice timelines and content requirements), Enforcement (CMPs — $127-$63,973 per violation per calendar year, capped at $1.9M per identical violation category), Transactions and Code Sets (standard transactions — 837 claims, 835 remittance, 270/271 eligibility, 276/277 claim status, 278 prior auth, 820 premium payment — all with mandated X12 005010 version, standard code sets — ICD-10-CM for diagnosis, CPT/HCPCS for procedures, NDC for drugs, CDT for dental, LOINC for lab orders/results, SNOMED CT for problem list)
regulations.hitech: Meaningful Use → Promoting Interoperability program — 2015 Edition Cures Update certification criteria, API requirements (FHIR R4 US Core 3.1.1/6.1.0 for patient and population services, standardized API with OAuth 2.0 authorization, patient access API — claims, clinical, pharmacy directory via payer-to-payer and patient access APIs, provider directory API), Information Blocking Rule (ONC/CMS — actors: health care providers, health IT developers, health information networks/exchanges, exceptions: preventing harm, privacy, security, infeasibility, health IT performance, content and manner, fees, licensing — each exception must meet specific conditions to avoid information blocking determination, civil monetary penalties up to $1M per violation for health IT developers/HINs/HIEs)

technology_architecture.integration_patterns: Healthcare integration engine architecture — interface engine (Rhapsody, Cloverleaf, Corepoint, Mirth Connect/NextGen Connect, Iguana, InterSystems Ensemble/Health Connect) as central hub for HL7 v2 message routing, transformation (v2-to-v2 field mapping, v2-to-FHIR conversion, X12-to-claim-object conversion), filtering (by sending facility, message type, patient MRN, insurance plan — only route relevant messages), alerting (message queue depth, failed deliveries, specific ADT events — patient merge, discharge, transfer to ICU), FHIR server (HAPI FHIR — open source Java, Microsoft FHIR Server for Azure, Google Cloud Healthcare FHIR API, Firely Vonk, Smile CDR — commercial, each with $everything, bulk export, subscription, graph definition support), terminology server (LOINC, SNOMED CT, RxNorm, ICD-10-CM/PCS, CPT/HCPCS, CVX (vaccine), NUCC provider taxonomy — each code system with OID, version, map sets (ICD-9→ICD-10, SNOMED→ICD-10), value set expansion ($expand operation), concept map translation ($translate)
technology_architecture.data_architecture: Clinical data repository — longitudinal patient record across encounters (demographics, allergies, medications, problems, immunizations, lab results, imaging reports, clinical notes, family history, social history, advance directives, care team), data provenance (source system, author, timestamp, facility, encounter, data entry method — direct entry, interface import, patient-reported, device), data quality (duplicate patient detection — probabilistic matching: name (Jaro-Winkler), DOB, gender, SSN last 4, address, phone with configurable match thresholds → potential duplicate queue → manual merge/unmerge with audit trail, overlay recovery if merged incorrectly), clinical data warehousing (OMOP CDM for observational research, i2b2 for cohort discovery, PCORnet CDM for pragmatic clinical trials, each with ETL from source EHR data and data quality assessment — Achilles Heel for OMOP).
technology_architecture.decision_support: Clinical Decision Support architecture — CDS Hooks (RESTful service discovery — CDS service endpoint registered with EHR, EHR calls service at trigger event with context, service returns cards (information, warning, critical, hard-stop) with links to SMART app for detailed interaction), knowledge representation (Arden Syntax — medical logic modules with data/evoke/logic/action slots for event-condition-action rules, FHIR Clinical Reasoning — $apply operation evaluates PlanDefinition/ActivityDefinition against patient context to generate RequestGroup of proposed actions), drug decision support (First Databank (FDB) or Medi-Span drug databases — drug-drug interaction severity levels 1-5, duplicate therapy classes, dose range checking by age/weight/renal function/hepatic function, pregnancy/lactation contraindications, geriatric Beers criteria, formulary status with alternatives, prior authorization requirements)

quantitative_benchmarks.healthcare_economics: US healthcare spending $4.5T (17.3% GDP), breakdown: hospital care 31%, physician/clinical 20%, prescription drugs 9%, nursing/continuing care 5%, dental 3%, home health 3%, other 18%, admin/insurance ~8%. EHR market $35B, telehealth $25B post-COVID (vs $3B pre-2020). Hospital IT budget 2.5-3.5% of operating revenue. Epic implementation: $500M+ for large academic medical center over 2-3 years. Integration cost per interface: HL7 v2 $10-50k build + $500-2k/month maintenance, FHIR API $50-200k build (first) + $5-10k per additional resource. Claims denial rate 5-10% of claims (industry average), cost to appeal $25-118 per claim, 90% of denials are preventable (front-end edits, eligibility verification, auth).
